description: The words this repository's shipped instructions use for one concept each. A concept has one preferred term; `forbidden` lists the variants that never name anything else, which no file of `clean` may carry; `counted` lists variants that are sometimes the concept and sometimes a plain use (the session's language, the agent's caller), which are counted and held by a ratchet rather than banned. A count is read over prose: frontmatter, fenced blocks, «…» quotations (a requirement's own words) and inline code (a file or identifier's name) are removed first, and a variant matches as whole words, case-insensitively. `scope` is every file whose prose a session or an agent reads as instructions, including what a script prints and what a schema's descriptions say, since both reach an agent. tests/test_terms.py holds the clean files at zero and every other file at the count tests/fixtures/term-counts.json pins; tools/term_counts.py prints and rewrites those pins. A skill whose SKILL.md defines terms under `## Terms` defines only concepts listed here.

concepts.means: whoever invoked the skill and decides what only a person decides
the subagent that writes the tests proving one task, named as its file names it
the session that runs a skill, addressed by the skill's text
a subagent that writes what a delivery is made of: task-implementer or test-author
send a subagent that has returned a new message in its own context, instead of spawning a fresh one
the invocation ends: nothing more is written, and the report says why
a script's non-zero exit naming what it refused
an invocation of another entry point, filled and ready to paste, that a report hands the person
